Check a CPUE model, overall and term by term

Source: R/check-cpue.R
check_cpue.Rd

Combine native fitting evidence, available model statistics, optional simulation-based residual tests, and exploratory checks for every model term. The report does not refit or select the original model.

Usage

check_cpue(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  residuals = NULL,
  simulate = TRUE,
  terms = NULL,
  nsim = 250L,
  batch_size = 25L,
  seed = 1L,
  component = c("auto", "combined", "encounter", "positive"),
  conditioning = "backend_default",
  residual_method = c("dharma", "simulation_pit"),
  residual_tests = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  dharma_max_mb = 256,
  trial_counts = NULL,
  response_transform = "identity",
  dharma_storage = c("auto", "disk", "memory")
)

# S3 method for class 'influ_check'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'influ_check'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'influ_check'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

model

A fitted GLM, GAM, glmmTMB, lme4, brms, sdmTMB, or single-response tinyVAST model.

data

Original fitting data, with original row names. Supply it when raw predictors are unavailable in the saved model frame (for example, poly(depth, 3)). Changed data fail alignment checks.

year

Original-data time column. NULL uses influ_residuals() time discovery. An explicit name must exist in the aligned data.

residuals

Optional precomputed native influ_residuals() result from this same fit. Reuses all stored values and tests, without simulation or recalculating missing tests. Backend, response, and observation IDs are checked, but old objects cannot prove identical fitted parameters; the caller remains responsible for same-fit provenance.

simulate

Calculate residuals when none are supplied? Default TRUE; use FALSE for a quick native-fit/term-inventory report. Missing residual checks are recorded as "not_assessed", not passes. A hard numerical issue also prevents automatic residual simulation.

terms

Optional subset of exact recorded term names. NULL includes every term. Interaction, auxiliary-component, and latent-process terms remain visible even when no valid univariate residual screen is available.

nsim, batch_size, seed, component, conditioning, dharma_max_mb, trial_counts, response_transform, dharma_storage

Passed to influ_residuals() for new calculations. No MCMC or original model refit is run. Compact DHARMa calculations default to bounded response blocks and a temporary disk cache; dharma_max_mb is a response-workspace budget, not a process-wide memory bound. Component selection is explicit for joint models.

residual_method

Residual engine for a new report: "dharma" (the checker default, requiring optional DHARMa >= 0.4.7) or "simulation_pit". This does not change the default of influ_residuals(). There is no silent fallback if an engine, family, or conditioning target is unavailable.

residual_tests

DHARMa-reference test set for new calculations: "none", "standard", or "full". NULL selects "standard" for DHARMa and "none" for simulation PIT. Full adds auxiliary quantile regressions and outlier tests, with additional computation, but no original-model refits.

alpha

Exploratory flag threshold, default 0.05. Term-screen p-values are Holm-adjusted across the calculated raw-predictor screens. Native DHARMa within-year p-values use their separately recorded Holm family; there is no universal correction across all different diagnostic questions.

x, object

An `influ_check` report.

...

Further arguments to printing or residual plotting methods.

row.names

Optional output row names.

optional

Passed to the data-frame method; retained for the standard [base::as.data.frame()] signature.

Value

A compact S3 influ_check object, with model_statistics, overall, term_checks, term_inventory, residuals, predictors, and metadata. base::summary() returns report tables; base::as.data.frame() combines all checks. plot(report) reuses the residual overview, and plot(report, type = "term", term = "depth") displays a retained raw predictor alongside its exploratory screen. Reports without residuals can still display the status table using type = "status".

Details

model_statistics contains available native sample size, likelihood degrees of freedom, log-likelihood, AIC, BIC, and deviance. Native GLM/GAM explained deviance and GAM adjusted R-squared are labelled separately; Bayesian R-squared is reused only when already stored. Missing quantities are NA, not fabricated or calculated by fitting a null model. Likelihood criteria are descriptive here: unlike table_criterion(), this function does not establish comparability between different fits.

Overall native checks distinguish numerical fitting issues from unavailable evidence. Term screens use uniform-scale PIT ranks: Spearman rho for a raw numeric predictor, or Kruskal-Wallis rank/location comparisons for adequately sampled categories. These are not DHARMa tests, coefficient-significance tests, tests of random-effect variance, or automatic term-removal rules. A raw-predictor check for poly(x, 3) is not a test of each polynomial coefficient. Native GAM smooth EDF/statistics are reported separately, not classified as residual failures. Joint/latent structures requiring an explicitly defined dependence check are reported as unassessed.

Optional uniformity/year/quantile tests use genuine DHARMa vector interfaces. Disk-based dispersion and outlier tests use labelled bounded-memory equivalents; dharma_storage = "memory" calls native object-based tests. The compact report retains statistics, implementation sources, and metadata, not that object's response matrix, the fitted model, or formula environments. Plotting and printing never repeat tests or consume RNG. Supplied residuals are compacted even if their original object retains native DHARMa simulations. Caller RNG is preserved during calculation.

"issue" denotes a numerical fitting problem; "review" denotes evidence worth inspecting; "no_flag" means only that the particular screen did not flag; "not_assessed" is unavailable/inapplicable-to-current-data evidence; and "not_applicable" denotes a genuinely irrelevant check or descriptive fitted-effect statistic. There is no overall model-pass flag. Correlation, fitting, posterior-data reuse, and simulation conditioning can invalidate nominal test calibration. A combined-response check does not validate encounter or positive components separately. No rotation, OSA, model-specific false-positive calibration, or hidden refitting is applied.

See also

influ_residuals(), table_criterion(), plot.influ_check()

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = factor(rep(2010:2013, each = 20)),
                x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 80))
d$y <- rep(0:3, length.out = 80)
fit <- glm(y ~ year + x, family = poisson(), data = d)
report <- check_cpue(fit, simulate = FALSE)
report
#> CPUE model check (GLM)
#> Overall model statistics:
#>  backend nobs df df_residual    logLik      AIC      BIC deviance
#>      GLM   80  5          75 -119.7865 249.5731 261.4832 87.46207
#>  deviance_explained adjusted_R2 bayes_R2 bayes_R2_sd
#>          0.02791429          NA       NA          NA
#>                                                                                                      method
#>  Native descriptive likelihood statistics; backend-specific deviance, not cross-backend adequacy or ranking
#>  notes
#>       
#> 
#> Overall checks:
#>                check         status statistic p_value p_adjusted
#>          convergence        no_flag        NA      NA         NA
#>             boundary        no_flag        NA      NA         NA
#>  finite_coefficients        no_flag         0      NA         NA
#>   finite_uncertainty        no_flag         0      NA         NA
#>             gradient not_applicable        NA      NA         NA
#>       residual_tests   not_assessed        NA      NA         NA
#> 
#> Model-term checks:
#>  term   component              check       status statistic df p_value
#>  year conditional residual_structure not_assessed        NA NA      NA
#>     x conditional residual_structure not_assessed        NA NA      NA
#>  p_adjusted
#>          NA
#>          NA
#> 
#> No flag is not proof of adequacy; unavailable checks are not passes.
#> Use summary() for methods, limitations, and suggested follow-up.
summary(report)$model_statistics
#>   backend nobs df df_residual    logLik      AIC      BIC deviance
#> 1     GLM   80  5          75 -119.7865 249.5731 261.4832 87.46207
#>   deviance_explained adjusted_R2 bayes_R2 bayes_R2_sd
#> 1         0.02791429          NA       NA          NA
#>                                                                                                       method
#> 1 Native descriptive likelihood statistics; backend-specific deviance, not cross-backend adequacy or ranking
#>   notes
#> 1      
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("DHARMa", quietly = TRUE)) {
  report <- check_cpue(fit, nsim = 50, seed = 42)
  plot(report)
  plot(report, type = "term", term = "x")
}
